svg.title: Nonce reuse: the keystream cancels out
svg.desc: Two messages are encrypted with AES-GCM using the same key and the same nonce, so they are XORed with the same keystream. An attacker who captures both ciphertexts XORs them together; the keystream cancels and the result is plaintext 1 XOR plaintext 2. If the attacker knows or guesses plaintext 1, here PAY ALICE 0000100, XORing it in reveals plaintext 2, PAY MALLORY 9999999, without the key. With GCM the reuse also leaks the authentication subkey, allowing forged tags.
svg.text: Same key, same nonce, two messages
Measured on the page: c1 ⊕ c2 == p1 ⊕ p2 → true; p2 recovered from a known p1.
1 Attacker sees only c1 and c2 on the wire
3 Guess or know one plaintext (formats are predictable)
4 XOR again: the other plaintext, no key needed
Fix: a unique nonce per key (counter or 96 random bits), or a fresh data key per object (envelope encryption).
